description: Prepare Quillhaven Academy's Daily Financial Health Brief as a draft for human review. Freshly reads the transaction ledger, budget targets and revenue snapshot Google Sheets (view-only), validates and normalizes every row, and writes a source-traceable report with posted / pending-confirmed / disputed-confirmed totals, prior-business-day comparison, month-to-date budget risks, revenue and an unresolved queue. Use when asked for the daily financial brief, daily financial health report, or operations-meeting finance summary.
---

# Daily Financial Health Brief

Produces the Finance and Operations Manager's daily brief for the operations meeting. The output is
a **draft for human review**: the skill is read-only, changes no source system, and never issues
payment instructions or takes a financial action.

## Inputs

| Input | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| Three Google Sheets URLs (ledger, budget, revenue) | Given by the Finance and Operations Manager. Order does not matter; roles are recognised from field meaning. |
| Reporting date | The Manager report request for the upcoming meeting. |
| Prior business day | The Manager report request; defaults to the previous weekday. |
| Attested ledger version (optional) | The source owner's completeness statement for the month-to-date ledger. |

## Run

Runtime: Python 3.10 or newer, standard library only (no install step). From this folder:

```
python scripts/run_brief.py \
  --source <ledger sheet URL> --source <budget sheet URL> --source <revenue sheet URL> \
  --reporting-date 2026-08-11 --prior-business-date 2026-08-10 \
  --attested-ledger-version ledger-2026-08-11-v2
```

Outputs go to `../deliverables/` (override with `--out`):

- `report.md` — the brief
- `normalized/transactions.csv`, `normalized/budget.csv`, `normalized/revenue.csv` — every source row in the required columns

Before publishing, the script prints each source's URL, spreadsheet id and title, tab, fetch time,
source version and row count, and writes the same into the report's Sources section.

## What the operator must do

1. Check the printed source lines: three roles, expected versions, plausible row counts.
2. Read `report.md` top to bottom. Anything under **Unresolved queue** and **Other items needing
   clarification** is a question for a person, not an answer.
3. Hand the draft to the Operations owner. Disputed refunds are flagged for their decision.

If the run fails (a sheet unreachable, a column missing, an invalid or contradictory row), the script
removes the previous deliverables and writes `deliverables/RUN_FAILED.md` with the reason. Do not
substitute a downloaded or cached copy; fix access or ask the source owner, then rerun.

## Reference

- `references/business-rules.md` — how every figure is derived and why
- `references/sources.md` — source roles, identities, validation and failure behaviour

   - Pipeline chain operators `&&` and `||` are NOT available — they cause a parser error. To run B only if A succeeds: `A; if ($?) { B }`. To chain unconditionally: `A; B`.

   - `>`, `>>`, and `Out-File` usually default to UTF-8 (with BOM) in this environment, but `Set-Content`/`Add-Content` still default to the system ANSI codepage — when writing a file other tools will read, pass `-Encoding utf8` explicitly to `Out-File`/`Set-Content`.

Before executing the command, please follow these steps:

1. Directory Verification:

2. Command Execution:
   - Always quote file paths that contain spaces with double quotes
   - Capture the output of the command.

PowerShell Syntax Notes:
   - Variables use $ prefix: $myVar = "value"
   - Escape character is backtick (`), not backslash
   - Use Verb-Noun cmdlet naming: Get-ChildItem, Set-Location, New-Item, Remove-Item
   - Common aliases: ls (Get-ChildItem), cd (Set-Location), cat (Get-Content), rm (Remove-Item)
   - Pipe operator | works similarly to bash but passes objects, not text
   - Use Select-Object, Where-Object, ForEach-Object for filtering and transformation
   - String interpolation: "Hello $name" or "Hello $($obj.Property)"
   - Registry access uses PSDrive prefixes: `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\...`, `HKCU:\...` — NOT raw `HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\...`
   - Environment variables: read with `$env:NAME`, set with `$env:NAME = "value"` (NOT `Set-Variable` or bash `export`)
   - Call native exe with spaces in path via call operator: `& "C:\Program Files\App\app.exe" arg1 arg2`

Unix commands that DO NOT exist in PowerShell — use the equivalent instead:
   - head / tail → `Get-Content file -TotalCount N` / `-Tail N`; piped: `| Select-Object -First N` / `-Last N`
   - which → `(Get-Command name).Source`
   - touch → `if (-not (Test-Path path)) { New-Item -ItemType File path }` (NEVER use `New-Item -Force` on a file — it truncates existing content)
   - wc -l → `(Get-Content file | Measure-Object -Line).Lines`
   - mkdir -p → `New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force path` (`-p` is not a PowerShell flag)
   - rm -rf → `Remove-Item -Recurse -Force path`
   - ln -s → `New-Item -ItemType SymbolicLink -Path link -Target target`
   - chmod / chown → not applicable on Windows; use `icacls` only if ACL changes are required

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

# Business rules

Established in the stakeholder interview with the Finance and Operations Manager
(`interviews/interview-r62mbg-20261012-1856.md`) and the Manager report request.

## Dates

- **Reporting date** is set by the Manager report request for the upcoming operations meeting
  (for the Aug 12, 2026 meeting: 2026-08-11).
- **Prior business day** is the comparison day named in the same request (2026-08-10). The script
  defaults to the previous weekday only if none is given.
- **Month to date** runs from the first of the reporting month through the reporting date.

## Daily totals

- Use only ledger rows **dated the reporting date** (or the prior business day for its figure).
- Keep **posted**, **pending** and **disputed** separate. Never net them together.
- A pending or disputed row is **confirmed** when it carries an actual numeric amount
  (`amount_status = confirmed`). If the amount is unavailable it is **unknown**: the amount stays
  blank, it is excluded from every monetary total, and the row stays visible in the unresolved queue.
- Signed amounts are kept as signed: credits and corrections (negative rows) reduce the posted total.

The five required figures:

| Figure | Rows used |
|---|---|
| Reporting-date posted total | status `posted`, date = reporting date |
| Reporting-date pending-confirmed total | status `pending`, amount confirmed, date = reporting date |
| Reporting-date disputed-confirmed total | status `disputed`, amount confirmed, date = reporting date |
| Prior-business-day posted total | status `posted`, date = prior business day |
| Change in posted total | reporting-date posted total minus prior-business-day posted total |

## Budget comparison

- Compare **month-to-date posted** spend by category against the Budget targets for the reporting
  month. Pending and disputed activity is not spend.
- Variance = MTD posted − budget. An overage is **material** only when it is **strictly above both**
  10% of the budget **and** USD 500. Equal to a threshold is not material.
- A **zero budget is a known baseline**, not missing data: any overage above USD 500 is material.
  A **blank** budget is unknown and is raised for Finance instead of assessed.
- A ledger category with no budget target is **unmapped**: shown in the table and escalated to Finance.
- A budget category with no posted activity is labelled **no observed activity**.
- Refunds carry the `review_all_pending_or_disputed` rule: every pending or disputed refund is
  surfaced for review regardless of size.

## Revenue

- Compare each revenue metric on the reporting date with the prior business day.
- Outstanding balance and payment plan balance are **separate dated metrics**. Do not add, subtract
  or reconcile them unless Finance clarifies their relationship.

## Unresolved queue

- Every pending or disputed row dated from the first of the month through the reporting date,
  including unknown amounts.
- The **Operations owner** reviews and decides each item. The brief never resolves one itself.
- Disputed refunds are called out explicitly (the manager asked that the USD 700 disputed refund be
  flagged for the Operations owner).

# Sources

Three Google Sheets, shared view-only by the Finance and Operations Manager. Each run reads all three
fresh through their CSV export (`/export?format=csv`, plus `&gid=` if the URL names a tab). Bundled,
downloaded or cached copies are never an input.

## Roles

Roles are recognised from the fields a sheet carries, not from its filename, title, tab name or
column order. A sheet must match exactly one role.

| Role | Identity | Required fields |
|---|---|---|
| transactions (Operations ledger) | `transaction_id` | transaction_id, date, account, category, description, amount, currency, status, source, source_version, amount_status |
| budget (Finance targets) | `period` + `category` | period, category, budget_amount, currency, owner, review_rule, source, source_version |
| revenue (tuition-system snapshot) | `date` + `metric` | date, source, metric, value, currency, source_version |

The revenue `source` column describes business origin; it does not create a second observation for
the same date and metric.

## Validation (any failure stops the run)

- Sheet returns CSV (a sign-in or error page means view-only access failed).
- All required fields present; no row wider than its header.
- Dates are ISO `YYYY-MM-DD`; budget period is `YYYY-MM`.
- Amounts parse as numbers (thousands separators accepted).
- Currency is USD for monetary rows.
- Ledger `status` is posted / pending / disputed; `amount_status` is confirmed / unknown.
- `confirmed` rows have an amount; `unknown` rows have a blank amount; posted rows are never unknown.
- Duplicate identities: identical repeats are counted once and flagged; **conflicting** duplicates
  stop the run until the source owner resolves them.
- The ledger has rows for the reporting date, and the budget has targets for the reporting month.

Blank-but-legal values (a blank budget target, a missing revenue observation) do not stop the run:
they are reported under "Other items needing clarification" and never filled in.

## Completeness

Operations states that ledger version `ledger-2026-08-11-v2` is the complete population for
1–11 August 2026 (recorded rows begin on 3 August). Pass that version as
`--attested-ledger-version`; if the ledger read returns a different version, the report says
month-to-date coverage is not verified and raises it for Operations.

## Failure behaviour

Outputs are written to a staging directory and only moved into `deliverables/` after every source
has been fetched and validated and the report built. On any failure the script deletes the previous
`report.md` and normalized CSVs and writes `deliverables/RUN_FAILED.md` with the reason, so a stale
brief can never be read as current.
